source: Not a book section. The shape (written plan, build with concepts injected where needed, playtest and reflection close) follows CodeHS's project modules in Introduction to Game Design; the grid-and-array game follows Video Game Design in JavaScript's Snake ladder. Structure only: no CodeHS text, problems or code is copied.

lessons.title: Plan, and a world on a grid
lessons.objective: Students will be able to plan a game as parts and remembered values, and place and move a sprite on a grid of cells.

lessons.title: Steering
lessons.objective: Students will be able to steer a grid sprite with direction variables, refuse a turn straight back, and end the round at a wall.

lessons.title: Growing and searching
lessons.objective: Students will be able to move and grow a snake by adding a head and removing a tail, and search the array to find a bite.

lessons.title: Playtest, check, and make it yours
lessons.objective: Students will be able to playtest their own game, link what they saw to their code, and extend it with a rule of their own.
